text:
Bitcoin held a fragile $58,000–$59,000 range Tuesday evening as markets braced for Wednesday's FOMC minutes and Thursday's June NFP report — the two most consequential macro events for crypto's near-term path. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish data-dependent stance, combined with May CPI printing at a 3-year high of 4.2%, has bond markets pricing a 60% probability of a September rate hike. The 10-year Treasury at 4.47% maintains peak opportunity cost pressure on non-yielding assets.

A structural divergence is emerging beneath the surface: while IBIT-led ETF outflows totalled $4.5B in June, on-chain data shows whales net-accumulated 270,000 BTC over the same period, pushing exchange reserves to 7-year lows. This classic supply transfer — ETFs distributing, large holders absorbing — has historically preceded cycle bottoms. The NFP print Thursday and the July 14 CPI release will determine whether the macro catalyst arrives soon enough to activate that latent demand.
